description: Minimizing the Impacts of Coastal Flooding Helps City Prepare for Sea Level Rise is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by City of Charleston; NOAA Office for Coastal Management; South Carolina Sea Grant. Several times per year, seawater floods some of the streets in Charleston, South Carolina. Taking steps to deal with this "nuisance" flooding can help the city prepare for sea level rise. Coverage: South Carolina (2014). The toolkit gives South Carolina as the location, 2014 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). outcomes: Residents of Charleston, South Carolina, are all too familiar with the periodic flooding that occurs during extreme high tides. During these events, salt water backs up through storm drains, resulting in hazardous road conditions. Traffic patterns are disrupted and motorists are forced to take alternate routes.
